title: 2023 AMC 10A Problem 11
statement: A square of area \(2\) is inscribed in a square of area \(3,\) creating four congruent triangles, as shown below. What is the ratio of the shorter leg to the longer leg in the shaded right triangle?

solutions.text: Each corner right triangle has legs \(a\) and \(b.\) A side of the outer square gives \(a+b=\sqrt3,\) and a side of the inscribed square gives \(a^2+b^2=2.\) Subtract to find the product: \(2ab=(a+b)^2-(a^2+b^2)\) \(=3-2\) \(=1,\) so \(ab=\tfrac12.\) Then \(a\) and \(b\) are the roots of \(t^2-\sqrt3\,t+\tfrac12=0,\) namely \(\tfrac{\sqrt3\pm1}{2}.\) The ratio of the smaller leg to the larger is \(\dfrac{\sqrt3-1}{\sqrt3+1}\) \(=\dfrac{(\sqrt3-1)^2}{2}\) \(=2-\sqrt3.\) Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Each corner triangle has legs \(a,b\) with \(a+b=\sqrt3\) (a side of the big square) and \(a^2+b^2=2\) (a side of the small square)
